Test Objective: Verify PCIe device enumeration by performing link training, cache coherency programming, link status polling, vendor ID read, command register configuration, memory base programming, BAR enumeration on both DM0 and DM1 instances, and synchronization handshake.
Test Description: This test validates the complete PCIe device enumeration flow. It begins by initializing the synchronization register and performing link training on the configured PCIe instance (DM0 or DM1 in RC or EP mode). Cache coherency control is then programmed on both PCIE0 and PCIE1 instances by setting the master AXI read/write cache mode and value fields via read-modify-write operations on the COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF register. The test polls the SII link status registers on both instances until the link is confirmed up (status bits 0xD1). In RC mode, the Vendor ID is read from the TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG, the TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG is configured to enable IO, Memory, and Bus Master access, and memory base programming is performed for both DM0 and DM1. System-level configuration registers are then written. Cache coherency is subsequently disabled by clearing the cache value fields. BAR enumeration is performed on both slave interfaces by writing 0xFFFFFFFF to BAR0_REG through PREF_MEM_LIMIT_PREF_MEM_BASE_REG, reading back to determine BAR sizes, then programming final BAR values. The test concludes by polling the synchronization register for a completion handshake value of 0x12345678.
Pre-conditions:
1. PCIe subsystem is powered on and out of reset.
2. PCIe link partner (RC or EP) is present and ready.
3. The compile-time mode flag (DM0_RC, DM1_RC, DM0_EP, or DM1_EP) is defined.
4. System integration interface (SII) registers are accessible.
5. PCIe DBI and slave configuration spaces are accessible.
6. Header file pcie.h with macro definitions and helper functions is available.
Test Steps:
1. Write 0x0 to the synchronization register to initialize the handshake.
2. Perform PCIe link training on the configured instance (DM0 or DM1) with x4 lane width.
3. Program cache coherency on PCIE0 instance: read the Coherency Control 3 register, set AXI write cache mode bits [14:11] to 0xF and read cache mode bits [6:3] to 0xF via read-modify-write, then set AXI write cache value bits [30:27] to 0xF and read cache value bits [22:19] to 0xF.
4. Repeat cache coherency programming for PCIE1 instance with the same bit field settings.
5. Wait for 20 cycles, then perform a consolidated cache coherency write on both PCIE0 and PCIE1 setting all four cache fields simultaneously.
6. Read the SII0 link status register and poll until link-up status bits (0xD1) are confirmed.
7. Configure non-secure protection via NIC programming.
8. Read the SII1 link status register and poll until link-up status bits (0xD1) are confirmed.
9. In RC mode: Read the TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG to retrieve the Vendor ID.
10. In RC mode: Write 0x7 to the TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG to enable IO Space, Memory Space, and Bus Master.
11. In RC mode: Execute memory base programming for DM0 and DM1 instances.
12. Write 0x1 to six system-level configuration registers for subsystem initialization.
13. Disable cache coherency on PCIE0: clear AXI cache value bits [22:19] to 0x0 while keeping mode bits at 0xF. After a wait, clear both value fields [30:27] and [22:19] to 0x0.
14. Repeat cache disable on PCIE1 with the same procedure.
15. Perform BAR enumeration on slave interface 1: write 0xFFFFFFFF to BAR0_REG through PREF_MEM_LIMIT_PREF_MEM_BASE_REG, read back to determine BAR sizes, then program final BAR address values.
16. Repeat BAR enumeration on slave interface 0 with the same write-readback-program sequence.
17. Poll the synchronization register until the completion handshake value 0x12345678 is received.
18. Call finish to end the test.
Expected Results:
1. Link training completes successfully on the configured PCIe instance.
2. Cache coherency control fields are correctly programmed and verified on both PCIE0 and PCIE1.
3. SII0 and SII1 link status registers report link-up status (bits matching 0xD1).
4. Vendor ID read returns the expected value (0x16C3 per spec reset value).
5. Command register is successfully written with IO, Memory, and Bus Master enable bits.
6. Memory base programming completes without errors.
7. System-level configuration registers accept writes.
8. Cache coherency is successfully disabled on both instances.
9. BAR enumeration on both slave interfaces returns valid BAR size information when written with 0xFFFFFFFF.
10. Final BAR address values are programmed and read back correctly.
11. Synchronization register reaches the expected handshake value 0x12345678.
12. Test completes with finish(0) indicating PASS.

Functional Area: PCIe DMA Write and Read Data Transfer
Test Objective: Verify PCIe DMA write and read data transfer across all four DMA channels (CH0-CH3) on the configured PCIe instance, including interrupt-driven completion handling, data preloading, BAR programming, and memory base configuration.
Test Description: This test validates PCIe DMA write and read operations across all four channels on the configured PCIe instance (DM0 or DM1 in RC mode). The test begins by initializing the synchronization register and performing link training. After confirming link-up by polling the SII link status register, the Vendor ID is read from the TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG and the TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG is configured to enable IO, Memory, and Bus Master access. BAR programming and memory base programming are then performed. The test waits for a synchronization handshake, then preloads source memory with known data patterns (0xC0DEBEED and 0xF00DDEAF). The GIC interrupt controller is initialized and all IRQs are enabled. DMA write and read interrupt masks are cleared by writing 0x0 to the DMA_WRITE_INT_MASK_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_MASK_OFF registers. DMA write transfers are then executed sequentially on channels 0 through 3 by programming each write channel and triggering the transfer via the DMA_WRITE_DOORBELL_OFF register, waiting for interrupt-driven completion after each channel. DMA read transfers follow the same sequential pattern on channels 0 through 3 using the DMA_READ_DOORBELL_OFF register. The interrupt handler reads the DMA_WRITE_INT_STATUS_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_STATUS_OFF registers, masks the lower 4 bits to identify the completing channel, and clears the interrupt by writing the status to the DMA_WRITE_INT_CLEAR_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_CLEAR_OFF registers.
Pre-conditions:
1. PCIe subsystem is powered on and out of reset.
2. PCIe link partner (RC or EP) is present and ready.
3. The compile-time mode flag (DM0_RC or DM1_RC) is defined.
4. System integration interface (SII) registers are accessible.
5. PCIe DBI and slave configuration spaces are accessible.
6. GIC interrupt controller is available and functional.
7. Source memory region at 0xE6000000 is accessible for data preloading.
8. Header file pcie.h with macro definitions and helper functions is available.
Test Steps:
1. Initialize the synchronization register by writing 0x0.
2. Perform PCIe link training on the configured instance with x4 lane width.
3. Poll the SII link status register until link-up status (0xD1 mask) is confirmed.
4. Read the TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG to verify the Vendor ID.
5. Write 0x7 to the TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG to enable IO Space, Memory Space, and Bus Master.
6. Execute BAR programming and memory base programming for the configured instance.
7. Configure non-secure protection via NIC programming.
8. Wait for the synchronization register to reach the handshake value 0x12345678.
9. Preload source memory with known data patterns (0xC0DEBEED for first 128 words, 0xF00DDEAF for next 128 words).
10. Initialize the GIC interrupt controller and enable all IRQs.
11. Clear DMA write and read interrupt masks by writing 0x0 to the DMA_WRITE_INT_MASK_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_MASK_OFF registers.
12. Program DMA write channel 0 with source, destination, and transfer length, then trigger via the DMA_WRITE_DOORBELL_OFF register with value 0x0. Wait for interrupt completion.
13. Repeat DMA write for channels 1, 2, and 3 using doorbell values 0x1, 0x2, and 0x3 respectively.
14. Program DMA read channel 0 with source, destination, and transfer length, then trigger via the DMA_READ_DOORBELL_OFF register with value 0x0. Wait for interrupt completion.
15. Repeat DMA read for channels 1, 2, and 3 using doorbell values 0x1, 0x2, and 0x3 respectively.
16. Verify the interrupt handler reads the DMA_WRITE_INT_STATUS_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_STATUS_OFF registers, masks the lower 4 bits, and clears interrupts via the DMA_WRITE_INT_CLEAR_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_CLEAR_OFF registers.
17. Call finish to end the test.

2. SII link status register reports link-up status (bits matching 0xD1).

8. GIC interrupt controller is initialized and all IRQs are enabled.
9. DMA write and read interrupt masks are cleared successfully.

12. Interrupt handler correctly reads status, masks lower 4 bits, clears interrupts, and clears GIC IRQ.
13. Test completes with finish(0) indicating PASS.

1. PCIe subsystem is powered on.
2. PCIe DBI controller registers are accessible on both PCIE0 and PCIE1.
